 Heartland travel agents share tips for smoother holiday travel 
 Local travel agents give tips ahead of holidays By Madison Orchard Published : Nov. 16, 2026 at 6:47 PM CST Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google CAPE GIRARDEAU, Mo. (Heartland News) - Last week’s FAA grounding served as a reminder that travel plans don’t always go as expected. 
 As the holiday season approaches, local travel agents say a little preparation can help travelers navigate common disruptions.
 Susan Berghoff, office manager at 1st Class Travel in Cape Girardeau, said the holidays are among the agency’s busiest times of the year.
 “We’ve got a lot of people that want to go cruise. We got a lot of people that want to go to the beach. We got a lot of people that just fly home for the holidays,” she said.
 Busy airports can bring challenges, including flight delays, cancellations and missed connections, Berghoff said.
 “I mean, it can be just about anything. You have a 50-50 shot; sometimes it goes perfectly, sometimes it doesn’t,” she said.
 Berghoff recommends arriving at the airport at least three hours early during the holiday travel season, noting that getting through customs can sometimes take longer than expected.
 Travelers should also pay close attention to flight announcements. If a flight is canceled, Berghoff recommends getting to the ticket counter as quickly as possible.
 Shannon Thompson, a travel agent with Elite Travel Inc. in Cape Girardeau, said airport personnel can help travelers find other available flights.
 “Once you’re at the airport, the airport personnel really do have all the control over your flight. They can see what has additional availability on other flights that day,” she said.
 Thompson also recommends travel insurance to her clients. It typically costs 4% to 10% of the total trip cost, though coverage and prices vary by policy.
 “Travel protection can assist you not only if you were going to have to cancel your trip prior to your departure, but for any of those issues that would arise while you’re traveling as well,” she said.
 Both agents said patience and kindness can go a long way when dealing with airport staff during a busy travel day.
 They also recommend packing a change of clothes and other essentials in a carry-on bag and downloading the airline’s app for real-time updates.
